title.narrative: Climate Adaptation and Resilience for South Asia

description.narrative: The objective of the Climate Adaptation and Resilience for South Asia (CARE) Project is to contribute to an enabling environment for climate-resilient policies and investments in select sectors and countries in South Asia. The Project has three components. 1. Evidence-based Climate Smart Decision Making component will develop platforms to enhance access to data for resilient planning and investments, including hazard and climate variability data, climate impact knowledge and other sector-specific data. 1.1. Expanding South Asia Region (SAR) Regional Resilience Data and Analytics Services (RDAS) subcomponent will support the development of a public domain data and analytics platform, namely the Regional Resilience Data and Analytics Service (RDAS) Platform to make climate-informed policy, planning and investment decisions for climate resilient development. 1.2. Strengthening national-level sectoral decision support systems (DSS) for the Participating countries subcomponent will provide support to enable the Participating Countries in developing or enhancing their respective interactive decision support system (DSS) platforms. 1.3. Trainings for Climate-Informed Decision-Making subcomponent will support policymakers and other users (i) within the South Asia region, in utilizing the data and RDAS platform for climate-informed planning and decision-making through the provision of trainings at the regional level; (ii) within the Participating Countries in utilizing the data and DSS platforms for climate-informed planning and decision-making in various sectors through the provision of trainings at the national and sub-national levels. 2. Enhancing Policies, Standards and Capacities for Climate Resilient Development component has the following subcomponents: 2.1. Advisory services for policy and investment interventions subcomponent will support the Participating Countries, to develop and/or strengthen evidence-based resilient policies, strategies and action/investment plans within the Participating Countries for mainstreaming climate resilience. 2.2. Promoting Climate Resilient Design and Standards for South Asia Region subcomponent will facilitate (i) the development of regional climate-resilient guidelines; and (ii) strengthen national and/or sectoral standards. 2.3. Implementation Support to Climate-Risk Management Solutions for Participating Countries subcomponent will support capacity building and technical support across the Participating Countries. 2.4. Innovation for Climate Adaptation and Resilience subcomponent will support innovative and disruptive technology solutions for resilience. 3. Project Management and Specialized Support component t will provide assistance for (i) the establishment and operation of the Regional Integrated Multi-Hazard Early Warning System for Africa and Asia (RIMES) Project Implementation Unit (PIU); (ii) Project implementation and supervision of Component 1 of the Project, (iii) monitoring and evaluation; (iv) Training; (v) carrying out of relevant studies for climate impacts and related interventions, inclusive and gendered practices in climate resilient planning and investments; and (vi) financing of Incremental Operating Costs.
To contribute to an enabling environment for climate-resilient policies and investments in select sectors and countries in South Asia.

title.narrative: Innovative resilient solutions crowd sourced through Climate Innovation Challenge and TechEmerge Resilience Challenge

comment.narrative: 7 solutions were crowdsourced for India under TechEmerge Resilience Challenge in collaboration with IFC. 16 solutions were crowdsourced for South Asian countries (except for Afghanistan) under the UKFCDO's PARCC Trust Fund. Another 16 solutions were crowdsourced through the Regional IDA grant.

title.narrative: Innovative resilient solutions crowd sourced through Climate Innovation Challenge and TechEmerge Resilience Challenge

comment.narrative: A total of 39 innovative solutions were crowdsource, including 16 under the Regional IDA grant, 16 under the UK FCDO PARCC window, and 7 through IFC's TechEmerge Resilience Challenge. The diversity of innovations from flood-forecasting tools and mobile agriculture apps to smart groundwater mapping and slope-stabilization technologies, demonstrates the project's success in leveraging private-sector and academic innovation for climate resilience. This performance underscores the regional platform's role as a catalyst for innovation, cross-country learning, and public-private collaboration on climate adaptation technologies

title.narrative: A regional-level resilience data and analytics services platform (RDAS) developed and accessible

comment.narrative: RDAS, a cloud-based, open-access, AI-enabled platform for storing, managing, processing, analyzing, visualizing, and reporting data to screen climate risks to inform investments, policies, and planning decisions for climate-smart development, was completed in December 2024. The following summarizes the 5 milestones achieved: Milestone 1: RDAS prototype completed in Dec 2021 Milestone 2: RDAS user interface created and available to be connected with existing/new DSSs since October 2022 Milestone 3: RDAS experimentally operational since October 2022 Milestone 4: RDAS has been connected to SAHF Knowledge Hub and DSSs supported by the project • Linked to SAHF Knowledge Hub thru DataEx, which facilities connectivity to ECMWF forecast • Provides observation/historical/forecast hydrometeorological datasets to various DSSs Milestone 5: RDAS fully operational The system can be accessed at https://rdas.rimes.int/

title.narrative: Sectoral investments supported to include climate risks and resilient design in select sectors

comment.narrative: RIMES supported the Bangladesh Weather and Climate Services Regional Project (BWCSRP; P150220) by developing an audio broadcasting system for disseminating the agromet advisories generated under BWCSRP. The other projects being supported are: Bangladesh: - Climate Smart Agriculture and Water Management Project (P161534) - Western Economic Corridor and Regional Enhancement Program (P169880) in Bangladesh Nepal: - DoR Project - DoLI Project. Limited completion was due to delays in design finalization, extended approval timelines, and competing national priorities. However, the preparatory work strengthened technical capacity and established models for integrating climate risks into future infrastructure investments.

title.narrative: Sectoral investments supported to include climate risks and resilient design in select sectors

comment.narrative:
RIMES supported the Bangladesh Weather and Climate Services Regional Project (BWCSRP; P150220) by developing an audio broadcasting system for disseminating the agromet advisories generated under BWCSRP.
ADPC has been preparing reports outlining recommendations to support the following investment projects: • Climate Smart Agriculture and Water Management Project (CSAWMP; P161534) implemented by the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE) in Bangladesh; • Western Economic Corridor and Regional Enhancement Program (WeCARE; P169880) implemented by the Local Government Engineering Department (LGED) in Bangladesh; and • Two transport projects implemented by the Department of Roads and the Department of Local Infrastructure Development in Nepal.
ADPC has not provided evidence demonstrating that its recommendations have been incorporated into these projects.

The result demonstrates strengthened regional cooperation and information sharing for climate-risk screening and planning.

Users in select sectors satisfied with decision support systems and tools developed under the project

comment.narrative: 81.7% of users expressed satisfaction with decision-support tools developed under the project, surpassing the 70% target. Feedback highlighted improved usability, accuracy, and timeliness of sectoral advisories in agriculture, transport, and disaster management. The result confirms that DSS products effectively responded to end-user needs and enhanced sectoral decision-making.

title.narrative: Districts receiving advisories issued by decision support systems developed under the project

comment.narrative:
By project closing, 153 districts across Bangladesh, Nepal, and Pakistan were receiving advisories generated through DSSs developed under the project, five times the original target of 30 districts. The breakdown is as follows: • Bangladesh (64 districts): agricultural and livestock advisories disseminated through the Bangladesh Agro-Meteorological Information System (BAMIS) and the National Livestock Advisory System (NLAS). • Nepal (42 districts): road, disaster-preparedness, and agriculture advisories issued through NAVIGATE (Department of Roads), READY (NDRRMA), and NAMIS/ADVISE (MoALD). • Pakistan (47 districts): advisories produced via ADVISE (Punjab Agriculture Department and Balochistan Agriculture College Directorate) and CLIM-PLANNeD (MoPDSI).
This strong performance resulted from the full operationalization of the RDAS platform and its linkages with national systems, enabling wider dissemination of early-warning products to local decision-makers and communities.
